metadata.title: [CHORE][SECURITY]: GrpcEndpoint.start() should enforce its own SSRF/TLS policy with explicit opt-out
metadata.author: jonpspri

description:
### 🔧 Chore Summary

`GrpcEndpoint.start()` in `mcpgateway/translate_grpc.py` opens a gRPC channel to an arbitrary `target` and (when `reflection_enabled=True`) runs reflection RPCs against it. Today the SSRF/TLS validation lives one layer up in `GrpcService.register_service()` and `GrpcService.invoke_method()` (PR #3202 added these).

That works for the manager-service paths, but **direct callers of `GrpcEndpoint`** — `expose_grpc_via_sse()` in the CLI translator, and any future consumer of the class — can construct an endpoint and call `start()` without going through the validators. The class-internal contract has no SSRF defense.

### ⚙️ Why now

PR #3202 surfaced this during deep review (review item #13 in the PR comment trail). The current behavior is "the manager service is the security boundary"; better practice is "every public method of `GrpcEndpoint` enforces its own policy and the manager service can opt out for trusted local CLI use".

### 📋 Acceptance Criteria

- `GrpcEndpoint.start()` accepts a `trusted_local: bool = False` parameter.
- When `trusted_local=False` (default), `start()` calls `_validate_grpc_target(self._target)` and (if TLS paths are set) `_validate_tls_path()` before opening any channel.
- When `trusted_local=True`, the validators are skipped and the call proceeds with a `logger.warning` once per process.
- `GrpcService.register_service` and `GrpcService.invoke_method` either pass `trusted_local=True` (because they validated already) and gain a comment explaining why, OR drop their pre-call validation since `start()` now handles it. Pick one to avoid double-validating.
- `expose_grpc_via_sse()` and `mcpgateway.translate_grpc` CLI entrypoints either pass `trusted_local=True` explicitly or call the validators themselves.
- Regression test: instantiate `GrpcEndpoint` directly with a known-blocked target (e.g. `metadata.google.internal`) and assert `start()` raises before `grpc.insecure_channel` is called.

### 🔗 Context

- Source: deep-review of PR #3202, item #13 in [PR comment](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/pull/3202#issuecomment-4386420357).
- Adjacent: #2663 (broader SSRF prevention epic) — this issue is narrower, focused on the gRPC client.
